texto:
This week, a U.S. Senate race in Mississippi came down to about a thousand votes, out of nearly a million cast.

Sounds tight? History has seen much worse.

New Hampshire, 1974. On election night, one candidate wins by 355 votes. The first recount flips it: the other man wins by 10. The second recount flips it back: a win by 2 votes.

The Senate itself took the case. Six weeks of debate. No decision.

So they did something rare. They declared the seat vacant, and New Hampshire voted again.

In September 1975, the do-over wasn't close at all: John Durkin won by about 27,000 votes.

Minnesota, 2008, was decided by 312 votes, after eight months of recounts and court fights.

So whatever happens next, it has happened before. The American File.
titulo: The closest Senate race in history came down to 2 votes #shorts
